descriptionChirho: To move toward someone or something, come near, draw close; the basic intransitive sense of physical or relational approach (Qal stem).
To advance or press forward with deliberate or aggressive intent, often in a military or confrontational context (Qal stem).
To approach or draw near in a middle/reflexive sense, often of presenting oneself before God, a ruler, or for judgment (Nifal stem).
Metaphorical extension: to overtake or catch up with, said of events, blessings, or curses reaching someone (Nifal stem).
To cause to approach, bring someone or something near; the general causative sense of bringing a person, animal, or object into proximity (Hifil stem).
To present or offer in a sacrificial or cultic context, bringing an offering or gift before God; a specialized causative use in ritual worship (Hifil stem).
Metaphorical causative extension: to cause to reach or overtake, said of calamity or consequence catching up (Hifil stem).

labelChirho: Hofal: be brought near, be offered
descriptionChirho: Passive of the Hifil: to be brought near or to be offered/presented, typically in cultic or formal contexts (Hofal stem).
To draw near in a reflexive or reciprocal sense, presenting oneself or approaching together as a group (Hitpael stem).
